name: Teledyne Technologies Incorporated
sector: Industrials / Aerospace & Defense electronics and instrumentation
moat_justification: Leading, vertically integrated positions in thermal imaging (FLIR) and other sensor niches, proprietary IP and defense-program qualification incumbency that is hard to displace, diversified end markets and proven pricing in Digital Imaging - but much of the portfolio is competitive industrial product, rivals contest the same defense programs, growth is partly acquired, and returns on capital are solid rather than exceptional; moderate moat, CAP 9.8y.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 28, 2025 (filed 2026-02-20, accession 0001094285-26-000017), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: 'Stock-based compensation' $39.6 million for FY2025, $37.7 million for FY2024 and $32.3 million for FY2023. EDGAR companyfacts carries the same expense only as quarterly/segment AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense facts (9M 2025 $30.7M in the Q3 2025 10-Q cash-flow statement matches), with no annual-duration fact under the engine's SBC tags, so the engine found no FY SBC for 2023-2025.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
one_liner: High-quality diversified sensor/imaging compounder, moat 6/10 - but at $607.91 (~25.8x TTM owner's earnings of $23.52/share) it does not clear 15%: weighted IRR 8.29%, weighted IV@15% $265.84; it clears the 15% hurdle only at ~$266, and nearer ~$190 (the bear-case IV@15%) with a margin of safety.
moat_for: Leading niche positions in sensors and imaging - FLIR is the thermal-imaging leader, vertically integrated from detectors/ROICs to full camera systems
Proprietary sensor IP and decades of qualification incumbency on defense and space programs - hard to displace once designed in
Diversified end markets (defense, industrial, environmental, marine, medical) smooth single-program cycles
Proven pricing power in Digital Imaging - Q2 2026 segment margin expanded on pricing and mix
Disciplined capital allocation: consistent OE, buybacks, and debt paydown (net debt down to ~$1.69B by Q2 2026 per the Q2 release)
moat_against: Much of the portfolio sells competitive industrial/instrumentation products with limited pricing power
Capable defense-electronics rivals (L3Harris, Leonardo DRS and primes' in-house units) contest the same programs
US government / defense-budget exposure and program concentration in funded backlog
Growth is partly bought, not organic - serial M&A carries goodwill and integration risk (FLIR is the big one)
Short-cycle commercial markets are cyclical, and tariffs / supply chain hit 2025-26 prints and guidance commentary
